items.headline: Apple's $299 HomeView smart display ships, but skips the EU over Siri AI rules
items.summary: Apple began selling its first Siri-powered smart home hub, HomeView, on November 13 for $299, with face recognition and home-control features, but the device will not be sold in the EU because the new Siri AI isn't yet available there. It's a rare case of a major AI-infused consumer device launching everywhere except Europe due to regulatory uncertainty.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO said to be multiple times oversubscribed ahead of Nasdaq debut
items.summary: Bloomberg reported that orders for Anthropic's 825 million IPO shares, priced at $70-$78 each, already run to several times the amount on offer, with pricing expected November 18 and trading to begin under ticker 'ANT' on November 19. A concurrent $26 billion private placement from Nvidia, Google, Microsoft and other partners underscores how central Anthropic has become to AI infrastructure spending.

items.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings and turns connectors into full in-chat apps
items.summary: Anthropic rolled out Claude Meetings in beta, letting Claude join Google Meet calls to take notes and act on action items, alongside generally-available 'interactive connectors' that open full apps like Adobe, Atlassian and HubSpot directly inside a conversation rather than just a preview. New Sheets and Whiteboards betas round out a push to make Claude a general-purpose office suite.

items.headline: Google DeepMind uses AI to formally verify Signal's encryption code
items.summary: DeepMind said its AlphaProof Code system generated several million lines of machine-checked mathematical proof verifying key security guarantees of the Signal protocol's one-to-one messaging, a task that took about four weeks versus years of human effort. When researchers reintroduced two previously fixed bugs, the system correctly flagged both builds as insecure, though the analysis didn't cover group messaging or the full mobile app.

items.headline: Google DeepMind launches Gemini Robotics 2.5 with a new jailbreak safety benchmark
items.summary: DeepMind released Gemini Robotics 2.5, its latest vision-language-action model for humanoid and other robots, with improved operator steerability and stronger resistance to adversarial manipulation. Alongside it, DeepMind published ASIMOV-jailbreak, an open benchmark for testing how robot control models resist being tricked into unsafe behavior.

items.headline: Meta launches Muse Ember, a cheap multimodal model built for AI agent subtasks
items.summary: Meta's Superintelligence Labs released Muse Ember, the smallest model in its Muse family, designed as a low-cost workhorse for high-volume agent subtasks like tool calls, coding, routing and document parsing. It accepts text, images, video, audio and PDFs, offers a roughly 1-million-token context window, and is priced at $0.10 per million input tokens, positioning it to pair with larger planning models like Muse Wonder.

items.headline: OpenAI to retire Advanced and Standard Voice modes in ChatGPT on December 11
items.summary: OpenAI notified users it will phase out its older Advanced and Standard voice modes, defaulting everyone to the newer GPT-Live voice model after December 11; conversation history carries over and live video/screen-sharing stays on Advanced Voice until GPT-Live supports it. The move consolidates ChatGPT's voice stack around a single, more capable architecture after user pushback to earlier voice changes.

items.headline: OpenAI winds down Cursor's access to its models after SpaceX acquisition
items.summary: OpenAI is cutting off model access for AI coding tool Cursor, now owned by Anysphere following SpaceX's acquisition, with the contract fully lapsing around November 12 and future OpenAI models withheld entirely. Cursor's CEO said OpenAI models made up only about 5% of its traffic, and users can still reach them with personal API keys.

items.headline: Nominal raises $240M to put AI agents inside hardware testing
items.summary: Hardware-engineering software startup Nominal raised a $240 million Series C led by Lightspeed Venture Partners at a $3 billion valuation, tripling its price tag from March 2026. The round, which follows a $71.2 million U.S. Air Force funding award in October, underscores continued investor appetite for AI tooling aimed at defense and industrial hardware development.

items.headline: Google commits $17 billion to a Wyoming data center as local pushback on AI buildouts grows
items.summary: Google announced a $17 billion AI data center in Wyoming, paired with a 702-megawatt natural-gas fuel-cell power project with carbon capture, that it says it will fully fund itself. The announcement landed the same week that most US data-center-related ballot measures nationwide passed in favor of tighter local controls, highlighting rising friction between AI infrastructure spending and communities hosting it.
